highlights.content: **TRENDING:** * [Webinar | What It Takes to Make AI Trustworthy in Healthcare](/webinars/webinar-what-takes-to-make-ai-trustworthy-in-healthcare-w-7192?rf=TB)• * [2026 Resilience Week NYC: Healthcare, Fraud, & Finance Summits](https://ismg.events/general/resilience-week/?utm_source=trending)• # AI Agent Governance Starts With Identity Autonomous Systems Need Distinct Identities, Limited Access and Human Owners [Jennifer Lawinski](https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/authors/jennifer-lawinski-i-7546) • October 9, 2026     * [Credit Eligible](/premium/pricing "As a BankInfoSecurity.com annual member, this content can be used toward your membership credits and transcript tracking.") ![AI Agent Governance Starts With Identity](https://ismg-cdn.nyc3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/articles/ai-agent-governance-starts-identity-image_large-4-a-33063.jpg) As AI agents gain authority to change systems, records and workflows, IT and security leaders need to bring them under existing IAM controls. (Image: Shutterstock) More enterprises are empowering artificial intelligence agents to act on behalf of the business, but the identity and governance systems needed to control them are evolving more slowly. **See Also:** [The Power of Three: Advancing Zero Trust Security](https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/whitepapers/power-three-advancing-zero-trust-security-w-16830?rf=RAM_SeeAlso) A new survey from cloud-based directory and IT management platform vendor JumpCloud [found](https://jumpcloud.com/resources/q4-2026-pulse-report) that 55% of organizations use or test agents capable of changing systems, permissions, records or workflows. But among the respondents whose organizations are using agents, 59% have not fully extended their human identity and access management policies to these non-human users. Forrester Vice President and Principal Analyst Andras Cser described AI agents as smarter, less deterministic APIs, and said that the combination of scale and autonomy at the enterprise level creates an amplifying effect. Enterprises can have significantly more agent identities than human users, and each may operate with more independence than traditional machines. But the challenge for CIOs and CISOs is figuring out how to bring agents into their existing enterprise identity frameworks before they gain more autonomy and take actions the business doesn't want. "The first and foremost important thing is to treat AI agents in the framework of existing identity and access management," Cser said. Agents are a new identity type, he said, but they shouldn't be managed through a framework completely separate from business users, administrators and existing machine identities. The process starts with discovery. Enterprises need an inventory of the agents operating in their environments, an approved pool of agent types and providers, and a process for reviewing the agent roster as capabilities and risks evolve. Each agent should also have its own identity and credentials. Those credentials should identify the agent while preserving its relationship to the human or system that authorized it. "There needs to be somebody at the end of the story," Cser said. "You cannot just say, 'We launched a bunch of agents from a script, and it did whatever it did.'" Enterprises need "personal, employee or workforce or customer-level accountability for agent actions," he said. The National Institute of Standards and Technology reached a similar conclusion in a recent blog post. Agents should be treated as "first-class entities" with unique identifiers, credentials and entitlements bound to the user or system operating them, NIST researchers Bill Fisher and Ryan Galluzzo [wrote](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/cybersecurity-insights/back-future-why-agentic-ai-needs-strong-identity-foundation). NIST warned against letting agents use shared human credentials, static API keys or long-lived bearer tokens. Operated by Terrasoft, Tab lets users send instructions via iMessage or WhatsApp for the AI to handle tasks like ordering food, scheduling, buying gifts, making phone calls, or paying bills. Independent benchmark testing showed Tab excelled in phone-call tasks and permission/privacy handling, but frequently failed in complex scenarios like cross-site restaurant reservations, travel booking, and online shopping, scoring 5.9 out of 10 and ranking 21st overall. Tab's debut comes as the personal agent sector heats up—Instinct recently closed a new funding round at a $10 billion valuation, while Meta and OpenAI have launched Muse and Dots respectively. Task execution reliability and user privacy protection will determine how far this category can go. ##### Key Elements US personal AI assistant startup Tab officially emerged from stealth on October 6, announcing a valuation of $300 million. The company went from offering services under the Tab name to disclosing its valuation in roughly six weeks. Against the backdrop of intensifying competition in the Personal Agent space, Tab's rapid rise reflects the capital market's strong enthusiasm for this category. Tab is operated by Terrasoft, Inc., a company founded approximately six years ago and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2020 batch. Terrasoft co-founder Benlloyd Goldstein served as the company's CTO from 2020 to 2025 and has since left the Tab team. Terrasoft has previously launched several consumer AI products. One of them, an AI Bible app called Faith, can turn Bible stories into videos, supporting voice features in 8 languages and text features in over 95 languages, reaching No. 12 on the US App Store's Books & Reference category. In 2026, the company began publicly promoting Flik, a generative AI tool offering an all-in-one workspace for video, image, audio, and copy generation aimed at content creators, with plans starting at $40 and $80 per month. Visiting Flik's website now redirects to Tab's workspace address. Tab's third co-founder, Ammar Amdani, was previously co-founder of Adapt Ventures, an early-stage tech investment firm. After Adapt Ventures invested in Flik at the pre-seed stage, Amdani joined the Tab team as a co-founder. In terms of product design, Tab's core differentiator from ordinary chatbots is its task execution capability. Users can send text, images, screenshots, PDFs, and video instructions to Tab via iMessage or WhatsApp, asking it to order food, arrange schedules, buy gifts, make phone calls, or pay bills. Tab has its own phone number, computer, and wallet, and can log into websites, fill out forms, make calls, contact merchants, and confirm with users before making payments. It can also connect to accounts like Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, GitHub, Linear, and Notion. In early September, Tab rolled out a series of features in quick succession, including WhatsApp integration, group chat support, browser operations, phone calls up to one hour, scheduled check-ins, and bank card payments. The product is updating rapidly but remains in closed beta. As an AI that can read emails, use accounts, and spend money on behalf of users, permission and security concerns are paramount. Tab's current approach separates login credentials from the AI and sets authorization scopes for each task. The system halts operations when it encounters uncertain transaction states. (Image: Shutterstock) More enterprises are empowering artificial intelligence agents to act on behalf of the business, but the identity and governance systems needed to control them are evolving more slowly. **See Also:** [The Power of Three: Advancing Zero Trust Security](https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/whitepapers/power-three-advancing-zero-trust-security-w-16830?rf=RAM_SeeAlso) A new survey from cloud-based directory and IT management platform vendor JumpCloud [found](https://jumpcloud.com/resources/q4-2026-pulse-report) that 55% of organizations use or test agents capable of changing systems, permissions, records or workflows. But among the respondents whose organizations are using agents, 59% have not fully extended their human identity and access management policies to these non-human users. Forrester Vice President and Principal Analyst Andras Cser described AI agents as smarter, less deterministic APIs, and said that the combination of scale and autonomy at the enterprise level creates an amplifying effect. Enterprises can have significantly more agent identities than human users, and each may operate with more independence than traditional machines. But the challenge for CIOs and CISOs is figuring out how to bring agents into their existing enterprise identity frameworks before they gain more autonomy and take actions the business doesn't want. "The first and foremost important thing is to treat AI agents in the framework of existing identity and access management," Cser said. Agents are a new identity type, he said, but they shouldn't be managed through a framework completely separate from business users, administrators and existing machine identities. The process starts with discovery. Enterprises need an inventory of the agents operating in their environments, an approved pool of agent types and providers, and a process for reviewing the agent roster as capabilities and risks evolve. Each agent should also have its own identity and credentials. Those credentials should identify the agent while preserving its relationship to the human or system that authorized it. "There needs to be somebody at the end of the story," Cser said. "You cannot just say, 'We launched a bunch of agents from a script, and it did whatever it did.'" Enterprises need "personal, employee or workforce or customer-level accountability for agent actions," he said. The National Institute of Standards and Technology reached a similar conclusion in a recent blog post. Agents should be treated as "first-class entities" with unique identifiers, credentials and entitlements bound to the user or system operating them, NIST researchers Bill Fisher and Ryan Galluzzo [wrote](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/cybersecurity-insights/back-future-why-agentic-ai-needs-strong-identity-foundation). NIST warned against letting agents use shared human credentials, static API keys or long-lived bearer tokens. AI Agents.content: [Skip to content](#content) [Madrona News](/insights/?show=madrona-news) October 9, 2026 # Highlights From the 2026 IA40 Summit: Harnessing the Value of AI ![Highlights From the 2026 IA40 Summit](https://www.madrona.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/0281-IA40-Summit-LR-scaled.jpg) This past week Madrona hosted its fifth annual IA40 Summit, where we celebrated the winners of the [IA40](https://www.ia40.com/the-list/) (the top 40 private AI startups as voted on by our VC peers) and heard from AI leaders and builders like [Rahul Patil](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rahul-patil-a0944836/) (CTO Anthropic) [Charles Lamanna](https://www.linkedin.com/in/charleslamanna) (EVP at Microsoft), [Swami Sivasubramanian](https://www.linkedin.com/in/swaminathansivasubramanian/?isSelfProfile=false) (VP of Agentic AI at AWS), [Zico Kolter](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zico-kolter-560382a4/?isSelfProfile=false) (OpenAI board member and co-founder of Gray Swan), [Thomas Dohmke](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ashtom) (former CEO of GitHub, now founder of Entire), [Jeanne Grosser](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeannedewitt) (COO of Vercel), [Carina Hong](https://www.linkedin.com/in/carina-hong) (CEO of Axiom Math), and many others. It was also our biggest summit yet with over 400+ attendees 🙂 This year’s theme was **harnessing the value of AI**. The conversation has moved past the model itself to the AI *system*: models plus tools plus agentic interfaces, wrapped in context and a flywheel of engagement. As our partner [Matt McIlwain](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matt-mcilwain/?isSelfProfile=false) put it in his opening remarks, “we’ve moved beyond, strictly speaking, token maxing.” Every layer now needs an ROI, and the questions of authority, agency, and accountability are no longer theoretical. The numbers behind the IA40 tell the same story. The 164 winners across six years have raised over $500B, and Databricks is the *only* company to make all six lists. Twenty-three companies are repeat winners this year, more than ever. Excluding OpenAI, Anthropic, and Databricks, which together account for 92% of dollars raised, the remaining winners have each raised over $800M on average. As always, we share our five key takeaways from the Summit here. ### 1. Agents Have Arrived Last year, we wrote that we were “heading toward an agent-first world.” This year, that world showed up. Across nearly every session, agents weren’t a prediction; they were part of how the speakers do their jobs today. The clearest evidence came from software engineering. [Eno Reyes](https://www.linkedin.com/in/enoreyes), co-founder and CTO of Factory, noted that autocomplete as the primary paradigm of AI-enabled development is only three and a half years old, and that last December there was a “renaissance” of developers downloading tools like Claude Code and Codex. Thomas Dohmke put it simply: “It’s never been more fun to be a software developer.” The shift isn’t limited to code. [Ryan Daniels](https://www.linkedin.com/in/crosbyryan/?isSelfProfile=false) of Crosby is building an AI-native law firm that sells fixed-price legal work, delivered by agents over email and Slack. Carina Hong’s Axiom Math has agents producing new mathematics at scale, including a new record on bounded gaps between primes. AI Agents.titleZh: Social Engineering AI Agents: The New BEC for 2026
AI Agents.content: * [Cybersecurity Operations](/cybersecurity-operations) * [Application Security](/application-security) * [Insider Threats](/vulnerabilities-threats/insider-threats) * [Сloud Security](/cloud-security) * [News](/latest-news) # Social Engineering AI Agents: The New BEC for 2026 As AI agents gain authority over business systems, attackers can manipulate them like business email compromise (BEC) victims. [![Picture of Alexander Culafi](https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt6d90778a997de1cd/blte0c88f087d1ad6f5/67c609df64f983454c3dd40b/1571751486317.jpg?width=100&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale "Picture of Alexander Culafi")](/author/alexander-culafi) [Alexander Culafi,](/author/alexander-culafi)Senior News Writer,Dark Reading October 9, 2026 7 Min Read ![A stylized human face represented via data, representing an AI agent.](https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt6d90778a997de1cd/blt509529652bae6ba5/6ac7de6c3ada349d7f093787/Digital_face-imaginima-GettyImages-2228383398.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale "A stylized human face represented via data, representing an AI agent.") Source: imaginima via Getty Images Cybersecurity Awareness Month traditionally focuses on teaching employees how to recognize social engineering efforts and how to avoid consequences associated with [business email compromise](/endpoint-security/attackers-combo-evasion-tactics-bec-phishing) (BEC). But as companies give AI agents authority to interact with business systems, threat actors can target AI agents and manipulate them into taking authorized actions instead — which should reshape how organizations train on BEC attacks. Consider a classic BEC scenario: an accounts-payable employee receives what appears to be a legitimate message from a vendor saying its banking information has changed. This tutorial walks through the full setup on Windows, macOS, and Linux, covers GPU acceleration for NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple Silicon, shows how to run Ollama inside Docker, hooks it up to a Python app and a browser chat UI, and ends with a complete working project: a local chatbot script with persistent memory that never leaves your machine. This pricing structure is highly attractive for high-frequency, repetitive decision-making applications at the cost level. ## **01** ## **Focus on Decision-Making, Filling the Capability Gap of Large Language Models** Different from traditional large language models that focus on text generation and complex reasoning, Microsoft-Decision-1 has a more focused design goal. **The Microsoft-Decision-1 model selects the optimal solution from preset options and assigns probability scores to each alternative answer, so as to help downstream applications determine whether to continue execution, retry, escalate processing, or submit for manual review.** (Microsoft-Decision-1 ranks first in accuracy and is the fastest model measured in actual tests) **Microsoft states that the model ranks first in accuracy across 36 benchmark tests covering nearly 150,000 questions.** Its functional positioning includes routing and distribution, content classification, task prioritization, result verification and workflow control, and can be seamlessly embedded into existing applications, AI agents and workflow systems. However, the above performance data comes from Microsoft's own benchmark tests, and independent third-party verification has not yet been completed. ## **02** ## **Internal Tests Show Significant Advantages in Speed and Cost** Microsoft emphasizes that each decision adds latency, especially when one step depends on another. For example, if 20 consecutive decisions are made and each decision adds 100 milliseconds, the entire workflow will add 2 seconds. The latency of Microsoft-Decision-1 P50 is 35 times that of GPT-6 Sol. (Time to generate a decision in a single request, the lower the value the better, taking the median of the JevBench test set) The **Xbox Research team** used it to classify more than 10,000 pieces of game feedback. The **Microsoft Copilot team** also found that the model performs similarly to GPT-5.6 Luna in AI response evaluation tasks. (When Microsoft-Decision-1 classifies the same text, the cost is only a few tenths of that of GPT-6 Sol) In terms of technical architecture, **Microsoft-Decision-1 is built on Qwen3.5-9B** and has undergone special post-training centered on single decision score. **Microsoft also plans to migrate the model to other bases such as its MAI series models and OpenAI models in the future...

AI Product.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Google, Unity Debut Spark, an AI Game Maker for 18+ [2026] ![](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/rcole.webp) [Ryan Cole](https://shattered.io/author/rcole/) Updated Oct 9, 2026 · 12 min read Google and Unity announced a strategic partnership on October 7, 2026, introducing an AI-driven path to building playable games without writing a line of code. The companies framed it as a shift in who gets to make games, not just how fast they get made. Unity’s press release described the effort as a platform for “the next era of interactive entertainment,” built around two connected products: Google’s experimental **Playground**, live immediately, and **Unity Spark**, a browser-based creation tool due later in 2026. The announcement lands at a strange moment for Unity. The engine maker is still working through the fallout of its 2023 pricing controversy, fighting an active lawsuit from ad-tech rival AppLovin, and trying to convince indie developers it has moved past the runtime-fee era for good. Pairing with Google on a no-code AI tool is a bet that the next wave of game creators will come from prompts, not from years of engine training. Whether that bet pays off will shape Unity’s business, and a meaningful slice of the broader [gaming](https://shattered.io/gaming/) industry, for the rest of the decade. ## What Google Playground Actually Does, and Why It Launched First Playground is the part of the partnership available right now. Per Unity’s own press release, it “allows users (18+) to generate and customize playable games using natural language prompts, with no coding required.” A user types a description of a game idea, and Playground turns that description into something playable in the browser, with further prompts used to tweak mechanics, visuals, or rules. > “Playground lowers the barriers to creation, so bringing game ideas to life can now be as easy as describing it through a few prompts, no coding experience required.” > > Google, company blog statement ([source](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/ai/playground-experimental-gaming-platform/)) That 18-and-over requirement is worth sitting with. Most mainstream game-creation tools aimed at casual users, from Roblox Studio to Fortnite’s Creative mode, skew toward teen and younger audiences. Gating an entire AI game maker to adults signals that Google is not yet confident in its content moderation for AI-generated output, or that it wants legal distance while the system is still labeled experimental. Google has not published a rationale for the age floor beyond calling Playground experimental. ## Unity Spark: The Full Engine Version Coming Later in 2026 Playground is the demo. Unity Spark is the product Google and Unity actually want developers and casual creators to adopt long-term. Unity’s press release says the company will introduce Spark as “an expanded creation experience,” described directly in the following statement. > “Building on Playground, later this year Google and Unity will introduce an expanded creation experience called Unity Spark, a brand new product built from the ground up for a new generation of creators.” > > Unity Technologies, company press release ([source](https://unity.com/news/google-and-unity-partner-on-new-ai-gaming-platform-for-the-next-era-of-interactive-entertainment)) Unity CEO Matt Bromberg went further in comments reported by GamesBeat, pitching Spark as a social creation tool rather than a solo hobbyist app. > “Today, together with our partners at Google, we announced Unity Spark, a new way for people to come together to make and share games right in their browser, no prior Unity or game development experience required.” > > Matt Bromberg, CEO of Unity ([source](https://gamesbeat.com/google-playground-and-unity-spark-will-enable-creators-to-easily-generate-3d-games/)) Running in a browser matters here. AI Product.content: [![GROW YOUR STARTUP IN EUROPE](https://novobrief.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/growyourstartup.png)](https://novobrief.com/grow-your-startup-in-europe/) [![novobrief Logo](https://novobrief.com/wp-content/themes/novobrief/assets/images/novobrief2.png)](https://novobrief.com) # Enterprise AI adoption is shifting from experimentation to engineering [NovoBrief Team](https://novobrief.com/author/novobrief-team/) - October 9, 2026 [![](https://novobrief.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image-1.png)](https://novobrief.com/enterprise-ai-adoption-is-shifting-from-experimentation-to-engineering/12029/) [![facebook icon](https://novobrief.com/wp-content/themes/novobrief/assets/images/icon-facebook-white.svg)](#) [![facebook icon](https://novobrief.com/wp-content/themes/novobrief/assets/images/icon-twitter-white.svg)](#) [![facebook icon](https://novobrief.com/wp-content/themes/novobrief/assets/images/icon-linkedin-white.svg)](#) As companies move generative AI from pilot projects into production environments, the challenge is increasingly about engineering rather than model access. Integrating AI into existing software, business processes and enterprise platforms requires organizations to address security, governance, reliability and long-term maintainability. AI agents are part of that transition. While businesses are exploring ways to automate tasks across departments, deploying agents in operational environments requires more than building a functional prototype. Systems must connect with enterprise data and applications, operate within existing controls and remain manageable as business requirements evolve. This shift is creating a larger role for engineering firms that can connect AI capabilities with the infrastructure companies already use. Instead of treating AI as an isolated initiative, businesses are looking at how it can become part of product development, platform modernization and everyday workflows. For AI providers such as Anthropic, partnerships with engineering companies offer a way to extend the use of their models beyond experimentation and into the systems that support business operations. ## **Anthropic brings Gorilla Logic into its enterprise AI ecosystem** Anthropic has named Gorilla Logic a Select Services Partner in the Claude Partner Network’s Services Track, positioning the engineering company to help enterprises integrate Claude into software products, platforms and business workflows. The designation is based on criteria including certified practitioners, customer deployments running in production and publicly available customer results, according to Gorilla Logic. The collaboration will focus on two areas. The first involves using Claude and Claude Code throughout the software development lifecycle to design, build, test and modernize products and platforms. The second centers on developing AI agents and automated workflows for departments such as finance, operations, compliance, human resources and sales. These systems can connect with existing enterprise applications through integrations that include the Model Context Protocol (MCP). ![](https://www.novobrief.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image.png) *Drew Naukam* For [Drew Naukam](https://www.linkedin.com/in/drew-naukam/?isSelfProfile=false), CEO of Gorilla Logic, the accessibility of AI tools is making established engineering practices increasingly important. “Anyone can build an agent. Which makes engineering standards matter more than ever,” Naukam said. “A lot of the companies we talk to already pay for Claude. What they want is help getting it into the work their teams do every day, in a way their security and IT teams will sign off on.” Gorilla Logic will incorporate Claude into client projects through Construct™, its engineering system of playbooks, reusable components, accelerators and tooling developed through two decades of delivery experience. The company works on digital product development, platform consolidation, application modernization ...

Open Source AI.content: # Jevman is a benchmark that uses probabilistic models specialized for rapid decision-making, such as Jev and GPT-6 Luna Decisions, to play Pac-Man. ![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/09/jevman/00_m.png) ' **jevman** ' is a benchmark that compares the situational decision-making abilities of AIs playing Pac-Man. It was released by Opper, a provider of APIs for AI, and compares the scores, decision-making speed, and execution costs of six different AI models, each playing Pac-Man 100 times. **jevman: a Pac-Man benchmark for decision models | Opper AI** <https://opper.ai/jevman-benchmark/> **GitHub - opper-ai/jevman-benchmark: Pac-Man driven by the jev decision model · GitHub** **<https://github.com/opper-ai/jevman-benchmark>** Jev is a type of AI developed by the American AI company TypeSafe AI. Unlike conventional text generation models, it specializes in evaluating choices and making decisions. While general large-scale language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT generate text, probabilistic decision models output the probability of each pre-set choice based on the given information. For example, it can show the probability of whether a customer inquiry falls under 'return,' 'technical problem,' or 'other.' Because it does not need to generate written explanations, it is suitable for applications that require quick decision-making. In Jevman, the AI model determines the direction Pac-Man should take each time he reaches a branching point in the maze. It's not just about picking up the dots in front of him; he also needs to consider the position of ghosts and escape routes, which tests the AI's decision-making abilities. Jevman evaluates the ability to quickly make appropriate decisions in a constantly changing situation, so a model that can arrive at the correct answer after thinking for a long time won't necessarily get a high score. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/09/jevman/01_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/09/jevman/01.png) Furthermore, jevman is designed to allow comparison of multiple models, including not only Jev, but also Kev, Laya, Clef, and GPT-6 Luna Decisions, within the same game environment. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/09/jevman/03_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/09/jevman/03.png) During the game, the AI model receives data in JSON format, including the maze structure, dot placement, and ghost positions. Based on this information, the AI model determines, with a probability, which direction (up, down, left, or right) to move in. The game then selects the direction of movement according to the returned probability. Specifically, the AI model is given a 2-second time limit for each decision. If it cannot answer within 2 seconds, a simple alternative algorithm determines the direction to proceed. The number of times this alternative algorithm is used is also recorded, so not only the accuracy of the decision but also the response speed is important. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/09/jevman/05_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/09/jevman/05.png) In the benchmark, each AI model plays 100 games against ghosts that operate under the same rules as the original Pac-Man. A game ends when all three lives are lost or 5 minutes have passed. According to Opper, the longest game that lasted in actual testing was 2 minutes and 24 seconds. The rankings are determined based on the average score of 100 games. However, because there is variation in scores from game to game, an error margin is calculated with a 95% confidence level as a guideline. Models whose score differences fall within this error margin are treated as having the same rank. You can also check the highest score for each model. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/09/jevman/04_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/09/jevman/04.png) On the Jevman official website, you can watch AI-controlled Pac-Man gameplay, and you can also control Pac-Man yourself and play against the AI. This tutorial walks through the full setup on Windows, macOS, and Linux, covers GPU acceleration for NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple Silicon, shows how to run Ollama inside Docker, hooks it up to a Python app and a browser chat UI, and ends with a complete working project: a local chatbot script with persistent memory that never leaves your machine. Everything below is built from Ollama’s own GitHub releases, official documentation, and model library pages, current as of October 9, 2026. Where a detail (exact Turbo pricing, for instance) is not clearly published, this guide says so directly rather than guessing, because a wrong assumption about memory requirements is the fastest way to crash a machine mid-download. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. [Add Now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Ftech-insider.org%2F) ## What Is Ollama, and Why Self-Hosting an LLM Still Makes Sense in 2026 Ollama is a local runtime for large language models. It wraps the lower-level work of loading quantized model weights, managing a GPU or CPU inference backend, and exposing a clean REST API, so a developer can run `ollama run llama3.1` and get a working chatbot without touching CUDA drivers or writing a single line of C++. The project’s core client and server have been open source since launch, and that has not changed with the latest release: the local software stays free, while Ollama layers a separate paid hosted option, Ollama Turbo, on top for people who want to run models too large for their own GPU. The case for self-hosting in late 2026 is less about saving a few cents per request and more about control. A local model never sends your prompts to a third party, keeps working when your internet connection does not, and does not change its pricing or deprecate a model string on someone else’s schedule. The tradeoff is upfront: you need the hardware, you manage the updates, and you are responsible for picking a model that actually fits in the RAM or VRAM you have. For teams already running local [GGUF-quantized models](https://tech-insider.org/gguf-model-quantization-2026/) or experimenting with [LangChain-style agent frameworks](https://tech-insider.org/langchain-vs-llamaindex-vs-crewai-2026/), Ollama is usually the fastest path from zero to a running local endpoint. What makes this a good moment to set it up is the model selection available right now. The Ollama library currently lists Qwen3 in both dense and mixture-of-experts variants (including the flagship Qwen3-235B-A22B and the newer Qwen3.6:27B agentic-coding build), OpenAI’s open-weight gpt-oss:20b and gpt-oss:120b, Meta’s Llama 3.1 family up to 405B, DeepSeek-V3’s 671B mixture-of-experts model, Go...

Expand Their Range of Applications" **"Although we were eliminated in the second round of the government's Independent Foundation Model evaluation, we will continue our efforts to develop Korea's top large language model (LLM)."** In a recent interview with The Asia Business Daily, Lim Jeonghwan, CEO of Motif Technologies, said, "We are disappointed to have been eliminated from the Independent Foundation Model project, but it was a good opportunity for us to grow as a startup and raise our profile. We will continue developing AI models by securing additional graphics processing units (GPUs)." [![Motif Technologies CEO Lim Jeonghwan speaks in an interview with The Asia Business Daily on September 21. Photo by Seo Sojeong.](https://cphoto.asiae.co.kr/listimglink/1/2026100815092955236_1791439769.png)](//www.asiae.co.kr/news/img_view.htm?img=2026100815092955236_1791439769.png "Motif Technologies CEO Lim Jeonghwan speaks in an interview with The Asia Business Daily on September 21. Photo by Seo Sojeong.") Motif Technologies CEO Lim Jeonghwan speaks in an interview with The Asia Business Daily on September 21. Photo by Seo Sojeong. [View original image](//www.asiae.co.kr/news/img_view.htm?img=2026100815092955236_1791439769.png "Motif Technologies CEO Lim Jeonghwan speaks in an interview with The Asia Business Daily on September 21. Photo by Seo Sojeong.") Lim said, "In our technical report, we directly compared our performance with leading open-weight models from overseas and confirmed our competitiveness in model design and inference efficiency: despite having fewer total and active parameters, our model achieved comparable performance. Unlike global tech giants, which invest massive amounts of GPUs and personnel, Motif achieved these results in about five months with a small team of 30 and approximately 800 GPUs provided by the government." Motif, a late entrant in the Independent Foundation Model project led by the Ministry of Science and ICT, made headlines in the second-stage evaluation held in August, ranking first among domestic models in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (AAII) assessment. Rather than fine-tuning overseas open-source models, Motif developed its model from scratch, designing it from the architecture up. It rapidly improved the model's performance, placing ninth globally among LLMs and among the world's top three open-weight models, attracting attention from developers overseas. Despite scoring highly in benchmark evaluations, Motif was ultimately eliminated and formally appealed the government's decision. Lim said, "I wanted to know the specific reasons for our final elimination, because I thought the issue concerned the company's credibility and reputation. In the end, the government did not provide detailed reasons, including about the evaluation process. By the next day it had pulled in roughly 2,956 stars in 24 hours and more than 10,400 total, according to GitHub trending data. The open-source toolkit is maintained by a developer going by morluto. It hands a coding agent the ability to decompile native binaries, Electron and JavaScript apps, .NET assemblies and even websites, then explain how a feature works without ever seeing the original code. It ships as both an MCP server and a command-line tool, so the same capability runs from a terminal or inside an agent session like Claude Code or Cursor. The pitch, laid out in REA's own README, is a three-step loop: decompile to recover readable code and naming clues, trace execution until the feature is explained, then recreate the logic in your own stack. Version 4.1, released shortly after launch, bolted on Android APK analysis through JADX and firmware analysis through Binwalk and Unblob, plus support for IDA Pro as an analysis backend. That's not a toy. JADX and IDA are the same tools professional reverse engineers have used for years: REA just puts an agent in the driver's seat. To its credit, the project is upfront about its limits. It doesn't claim to recover original source code or clone a whole application wholesale, and its documentation says every conclusion comes with evidence and stated caveats attached. Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#content "Skip to content") [![ FourWeekMBA](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20500%20166'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://fourweekmba.com/) [FourWeekMBA](https://fourweekmba.com/) The Leading Source of Insights On Business Model Strategy & Tech Business Models, and a Top AI Business News Publication [![ FourWeekMBA](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20500%20166'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://fourweekmba.com/) [FourWeekMBA](https://fourweekmba.com/) The Leading Source of Insights On Business Model Strategy & Tech Business Models, and a Top AI Business News Publication ![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%201024%20538'%3E%3C/svg%3E) # AWS Releases Open-Source Physical AI Toolchain for Robots [AI Business Brief](https://fourweekmba.com/category/ai-business-brief/) / By [Gennaro Cuofano](https://fourweekmba.com/author/thefourweekmbateam/ "View all posts by Gennaro Cuofano") / October 9, 2026 AWS introduced the Physical AI Toolchain on [AWS](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-aws-platform-business-model/) in a blog post dated 7 October 2026, and Amazon’s post of 8 October 2026 describes it as an open-source stack for building machines that perceive, reason and act in the real world. [Amazon](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-business-model "Amazon") says it is built on [AWS](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-aws-platform-business-model/) using NVIDIA’s physical AI stack, for industrial automation, autonomous mobility and humanoid robotics. The code sits in a public GitHub repository, aws-samples/sample-the-physical-ai-toolchain-on-aws, which the GitHub API lists under the Apache License 2.0. Business Pill · DATA FLYWHEEL A short explainer of the data [flywheel](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-flywheel "flywheel"): usage produces data that improves the [product](https://fourweekmba.com/product-management/ "product"), which brings more usage. It teaches the general idea only and says nothing about any company in this [story](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-story-generator/ "story"). **The key insight:** As we read it, [AWS](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-aws-platform-business-model/) is giving away the integration work rather than the compute. The repository is listed under Apache 2.0, and the blog says the pipeline it packages deploys on [AWS](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-aws-platform-business-model/) managed services, from SageMaker training to IoT Greengrass at the edge. Table of Contents [Toggle](#) ## What AWS Built The [AWS](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-aws-platform-business-model/) blog calls the toolchain “a publicly available collection of reference architectures, Infrastructure as Code, and deployment automation” for the Physical AI development lifecycle. It says the toolchain is robot-agnostic and task-agnostic: teams bring their own URDF robot description, teleoperation data and task definition. Amazon’s post lists five pillars: synthetic data generation, [model](https://fourweekmba.com/what-is-a-business-model/ "model") training, simulation and validation, edge deployment, and continuous improvement, where operational data from deployed machines flows back to generate new training data. On the [AWS](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-aws-platform-business-model/) side, [Amazon](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-business-model "Amazon") names [Amazon](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-business-model "Amazon") SageMaker for [model](https://fourweekmba.com/what-is-a-business-model/ "model") training, [Amazon](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-business-model "Amazon") EC2 GPU instances for simulation, [AWS](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-aws-platform-business-model/) IoT Greengrass for edge deployment and [Amazon](https://fourweekmba.com/amazon-business-model "Amazon") Bedrock AgentCore for orchestration. That also makes it an AI stock. But is Nvidia the best artificial intelligence (AI) chip stock to hold for the next decade? Let's dig in to find out. ![Artist rendering of AI chip.](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Feditorial%2Fimages%2F889150%2Fgettyimages-1402452876.jpg&w=3840&op=resize) Image source: Getty Images. ## Nvidia I think Nvidia remains a strong option in the [semiconductor space](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/information-technology/semiconductor-stocks/). The company's leadership in the AI model training segment of the market, with its graphics processing units (GPUs), is unquestioned, while it has transformed itself into a complete AI infrastructure player. At the same time, the stock remains cheap, trading at a [forward P/E](https://www.fool.com/terms/f/forward-pe/) of just 15 times fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028) analyst estimates. ![Nvidia Stock Quote](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Fart%2Fcompanylogos%2Fmark%2FNVDA.png&w=128&op=resize) ## [NASDAQ: NVDA](/quote/nasdaq/nvda/) Premium Feature Moneyball Superscore 95/100 Today's Change (-2.94%) $-6.99 Current Price ### Key Data Points Market Cap $5.6TMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Nvidia's growth is set to continue and outpace AMD's. **Nvidia**(NASDAQ: NVDA) and **Advanced Micro Devices** (NASDAQ: AMD) are two of the biggest names in AI computing. While Nvidia holds a larger market share and was the first to dominate the AI computing space, AMD has emerged as a viable competitor in recent months. In 2026, AMD's stock has outperformed Nvidia's, rising about 200% compared to Nvidia's 30% rise. But the past is in the past. Which stock has more upside in the future? Let's take a look at what's going on with these two and see which one makes the most sense for your investment dollars. ***Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger.** Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. When a stock triples in a year, it has a tendency to become overvalued, as a ton of future growth expectations are pulled into it. That's exactly what has happened with AMD, as it has gotten pretty pricey. AMD's [forward price-to-earnings ratio](https://www.fool.com/terms/f/forward-pe/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=127cdc17-a0ca-4730-9b21-dedcc0fd20f9) has taken off over the past six months, with another rally in recent weeks. This rally was triggered by AMD announcing a 10% price hike in mid-September. However, AMD shares are more than triple the price tag of Nvidia shares, and that is the biggest red flag for it right now. Essentially, a single Nvidia share represents over three times as much of the company as an AMD share does. This is an issue, as Nvidia is still growing faster than AMD is. ## AMD still doesn't compare to Nvidia With how well AMD has done in 2026, you'd think it would be crushing Nvidia, but it's not. During the second quarter, Nvidia's data center divisions grew at a 117% pace to $89 billion. Overall, revenue growth was 106% year over year to $96 billion. AMD's business is far more diversified than Nvidia's, and it isn't as concentrated in data center revenue as Nvidia is. This is hurting AMD's overall results, as it grew 50% year over year to $11.5 billion. TAIPEI, Oct. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Senao Networks Inc. today announced the launch of its new x86 enterprise server portfolio, featured on the company's Senao Computing website at [www.senaocomputing.com](https://www.senaocomputing.com/). [![Senao Computing's new x86 enterprise server portfolio spans data center and edge deployments, with NVIDIA RTX GPU support in selected configurations.](https://mmx.prnasia.com/media/MS2005177/20261008085852EDT_image_1.jpg?id=OA2995295&p=medium600 "Senao Computing's new x86 enterprise server portfolio spans data center and edge deployments, with NVIDIA RTX GPU support in selected configurations.")](https://mmx.prnasia.com/media/MS2005177/20261008085852EDT_image_1.jpg?id=OA2995295&p=medium600) Senao Computing's new x86 enterprise server portfolio spans data center and edge deployments, with NVIDIA RTX GPU support in selected configurations. The portfolio, which includes the SR810, SR710, SR610, SE210, and SE110, is designed to support a broad range of enterprise computing and AI workloads, including generative AI, AI inference, model fine-tuning, data analytics, visualization, and intelligent edge computing. NVIDIA RTX GPU support is available in selected configurations. **Bringing AI Closer to Enterprise Data** As enterprises accelerate AI adoption, organizations increasingly need computing infrastructure that can address different workload requirements while maintaining greater control over sensitive corporate data. Senao Networks' scalable x86 platforms allow enterprises to deploy computing resources according to their workload, performance, and deployment requirements. For organizations that prefer to operate AI applications within their own IT environments, on-premises deployment can provide greater control over enterprise data, infrastructure, security policies, and AI workloads. Meeting data governance and regulatory requirements depends on the deployment, operational controls, and applicable rules. *"Enterprises are looking for practical ways to bring AI closer to their data and business operations," said Dr. Bou Lin, President at Senao Networks Inc.
